paras.en: KAHN: It was - you know, he wasn't as warmly embraced in Mexico as Leo was welcomed in Peru. And I think people, Catholic or not, during Leo's trip really just wanted to feel hopeful.
paras.zh: 卡恩：你知道，他在墨西哥并没有像利奥在秘鲁那样受到热烈欢迎。我认为人们，无论是否是天主教徒，在利奥的旅行中真的只是想感到充满希望。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: So I want to turn here to Brazil's election, and here you are again on October 4, when the first round had just finished.
paras.zh: 施密茨：我想谈谈巴西的选举，10 月 4 日，第一轮选举刚刚结束。

paras.en: KAHN: Lula will have to find a way to close the gap in this runoff. He's not going to really be able to win over the 8% of voters who went for the other candidates. They were far-right and right, and their voters will fall in line with Bolsonaro, not with Lula.
paras.zh: 卡恩：卢拉必须找到一种方法来缩小这次决选的差距。他不可能真正赢得支持其他候选人的 8% 的选民的支持。他们是极右翼和右翼，他们的选民将与博尔索纳罗站在一起，而不是与卢拉站在一起。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: So, Carrie , I mean, you can hear in your reporting here that Lula was facing long odds. And in fact, no one in modern Brazilian history had come back to win a second round after coming in second place in the first round. In the three weeks that followed, was it easy to see where this was going?
paras.zh: 施密茨：嘉莉，我的意思是，你可以在你的报道中听到卢拉面临着很大的困难。事实上，在巴西现代历史上，还没有人在第一轮获得第二名后再次赢得第二轮比赛。在接下来的三周里，是否很容易看出事情的发展方向？

paras.en: KAHN: OK, I would totally be lying if I told you that I perceived this changing landscape or a huge political shift. I did not.
paras.zh: 卡恩：好吧，如果我告诉你我看到了这种不断变化的景观或巨大的政治转变，那我完全是在撒谎。我没有。

paras.en: KAHN: (Laughter) I just - I actually - you know, I thought Bolsonaro had it, you know, on election night. Where was I? I was in Brasilia at Bolsonaro's headquarters, waiting for him to come out...
paras.zh: 卡恩：（笑声）我只是 - 事实上 - 你知道，我以为博尔索纳罗在选举之夜获得了它。我当时在哪儿？我在巴西利亚博尔索纳罗的总部，等待他出来......

paras.en: KAHN: ...You know, with the hundreds of other reporters. It wasn't just me, but - that were waiting for him to give his victory speech.
paras.zh: 卡恩：……你知道，还有数百名其他记者。不只是我，还有——正在等待他发表胜利演讲。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: I want to ask you a question just about covering South America as NPR's correspondent there. You know, when I was NPR's Shanghai correspondent - I was in charge of covering China - I would have this map of China, and I'd put pins in different parts of China that I went to or reported from just to make sure that I was covering the entire country of China because it's such a diverse country when you actually zoom in.
paras.zh: 施密茨：我想问你一个关于作为 NPR 记者报道南美洲的问题。你知道，当我担任 NPR 驻上海记者时，我负责报道中国，我会有这张中国地图，我会在我去过或报道过的中国不同地区贴上图钉，以确保我报道了整个中国，因为当你真正放大时，这是一个如此多元化的国家。

paras.en: You are covering an entire continent. What is your approach to make sure that you're covering the stories that our audience needs to hear without trying to cover, you know, every story out there?
paras.zh: 您正在覆盖整个大陆。您采取什么方法来确保您报道的是我们的观众需要听到的故事，而不是试图报道那里的每个故事？

paras.en: KAHN: I guess maybe I have to go get some pins.
paras.zh: 卡恩：我想也许我得去拿一些别针。

paras.en: KAHN: See if I'm really covering all over the place.
paras.zh: 卡恩：看看我是否真的覆盖了所有地方。

paras.en: KAHN: You know, it's tough. It's daunting. The continent is huge. I can travel a full day by plane and still be in Brazil. It's amazing.
paras.zh: 卡恩：你知道，这很难。这是令人畏惧的。大陆很大。我可以乘坐飞机旅行一整天，但仍然留在巴西。太棒了。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: ...Just to stay in the same country.
paras.zh: 施密茨：……只是为了留在同一个国家。

paras.en: KAHN: To get to the Amazon, you have to take...
paras.zh: 卡恩：要到达亚马逊，你必须……

paras.en: KAHN: You have to take, like, two or three planes, and they don't fly all the time, and it's costly, and it's time-consuming.
paras.zh: 卡恩：你必须乘坐两到三架飞机，而且它们不会一直飞行，而且成本高昂，而且耗时。

paras.en: KAHN: I don't know. I always have to think about, will this story interest Americans? Under Trump - Trump 1 and Trump 2 - we do spend a lot of time, you know, covering what he is doing in Latin America. And, you know, in the second term, his administration has flexed so much U.S. power in the region that we're not - we haven't seen in decades.
paras.zh: 卡恩：我不知道。我总是要思考，这个故事会引起美国人的兴趣吗？在特朗普领导下——特朗普一号和特朗普二号——我们确实花了很多时间，你知道，报道他在拉丁美洲所做的事情。而且，你知道，在第二个任期内，他的政府在该地区展示了如此多的美国力量，这是我们几十年来从未见过的。

paras.en: KAHN: So it's all new. And so that kind of pushes the agenda a lot, you know, from seizing Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela and the U.S. now pretty much running the country. And now I can get visas to go in there. You couldn't get visas before. It was very difficult.
paras.zh: 卡恩：所以这都是新的。因此，从在委内瑞拉逮捕尼古拉斯·马杜罗到美国现在几乎在管理这个国家，这极大地推动了议程。现在我可以拿到签证去那里了。之前是拿不到签证的。这是非常困难的。

paras.en: KAHN: Yeah. There's rising gang violence and organized crime infiltrations all over the continent, so there's plenty to cover. And as you know, you know, you just work with a lot of amazing local journalists throughout the continent, in every country.
paras.zh: 卡恩：是的。整个非洲大陆的帮派暴力和有组织犯罪渗透不断增加，因此有很多内容需要报道。正如你所知，你知道，你只是与整个非洲大陆每个国家的许多出色的当地记者合作。

paras.en: KAHN: I just had a great time with a journalist in Uruguay that I've never worked with before and my regular producer in Peru. And we spent a lot of time brainstorming some stories that we could work on in the future, so there's no shortage in the continent.
paras.zh: 卡恩：我刚刚在乌拉圭与一位我以前从未合作过的记者以及我在秘鲁的常规制片人度过了一段愉快的时光。我们花了很多时间集思广益，集思广益一些我们将来可以制作的故事，所以非洲大陆并不缺乏。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: So, Carrie, you've been covering Latin America and beyond, and I'm just curious. Do you ever get homesick?
paras.zh: 施密茨：嘉莉，你一直在报道拉丁美洲及其他地区，我只是很好奇。你有想家的时候吗？

paras.en: KAHN: Of course. I don't know. I haven't lived in the U.S. for 20 years. I guess I do. For the U.S. - I'm from Northern California. Well, actually I grew up in Southern California, but I lived a lot of my life in Northern California. My kids are there, so yes, I would love to go back. My home is also in Mexico, where I have a lot of family. I don't know. I feel very comfortable in Latin America, and it feels like home.
paras.zh: 卡恩：当然。我不知道。我已经 20 年没有在美国生活了。我想是的。对于美国 - 我来自北加州。嗯，实际上我在南加州长大，但我大部分时间都在北加州生活。我的孩子们在那里，所以是的，我很想回去。我的家也在墨西哥，那里有很多家人。我不知道。我在拉丁美洲感觉很舒服，感觉像家一样。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: That is NPR South America correspondent Carrie Kahn. Carrie, thank you so much.
paras.zh: 施密茨：我是 NPR 南美记者 Carrie Kahn。嘉莉，非常感谢你。

articles.title: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?
articles.author: Rob Schmitz

paras.en: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?
paras.zh: 习近平在深圳峰会上与特朗普的熊抱得到了什么？

paras.en: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Robert Daly, director of the program on US China relations at University of Maryland's School of Public Policy, about President Trump's trip to China this week.
paras.zh: 美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 的罗布·施密茨 (Rob Schmitz) 与马里兰大学公共政策学院美中关系项目主任罗伯特·戴利 (Robert Daly) 就特朗普总统本周的中国之行进行了交谈。

paras.en: When the president goes on a big diplomatic trip, it's not always clear what's happening in all those meetings they go to. That was true during President Trump's trip to China this week, but there were intriguing public moments.
paras.zh: 当总统进行一次大型外交访问时，人们并不总是清楚他们参加的所有会议中发生了什么。特朗普总统本周访华期间确实如此，但也有一些有趣的公开时刻。

paras.en: UNIDENTIFIED CHILDREN: (Chanting in non-English language).
paras.zh: 身份不明的儿童：（用非英语语言念诵）。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: A group of children chanted, warm welcome, over and over, as Xi Jinping met Trump on the tarmac. Now add a third leader to the mix.
paras.zh: 施密茨：当习近平在停机坪上会见特朗普时，一群孩子一遍又一遍地高喊着热烈欢迎的口号。现在添加第三位领导者。

paras.en: PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: Who is he? He's my friend.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统：他是谁？他是我的朋友。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: That was Vladimir Putin, who's also a friend of Xi Jinping's, though the two may preside over an uneasy alliance. The stakes were high. Trump is looking for a breakthrough on nuclear weapons control. The U.S. and China are in a faceoff over AI, and a deal to end the bloodshed in Ukraine has been elusive.
paras.zh: 施密茨：那是弗拉基米尔·普京，他也是习近平的朋友，尽管两人的联盟可能并不稳固。赌注很高。特朗普正在寻求核武器控制方面的突破。美国和中国在人工智能问题上陷入对峙，结束乌克兰流血事件的协议一直难以达成。

paras.en: Now that the summit's over, we're joined by someone who can help make sense of what happened. Robert Daly was a U.S. foreign service officer in China and now directs the program on U.S.-China relations at the University of Maryland School of Public Policy. And he's here with me in the studio. Welcome.
paras.zh: 现在峰会已经结束了，有人可以帮助我们了解所发生的事情。罗伯特·戴利（Robert Daly）曾是美国驻华外交官员，现在马里兰大学公共政策学院负责美中关系项目。他和我一起在工作室里。欢迎。

paras.en: ROBERT DALY: Good to be here. Thank you.
paras.zh: 罗伯特·戴利：很高兴来到这里。谢谢。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: So what did Xi Jinping want out of this meeting?
paras.zh: 施密茨：那么习近平想从这次会议中得到什么？

paras.en: DALY: Xi Jinping - as always, his first goal is performative. It is to have the Chinese people see him as a world leader, beneficent, competent, hosting others who are coming somewhat cap in hand, at least in a very friendly way, to China. There's a very ancient saying in Chinese, (speaking Chinese), which means the 10,000 kingdoms all come to the center here. And Xi has been hosting an awful lot of leaders recently.
paras.zh: 达利：习近平——一如既往，他的首要目标是表演。让中国人民将他视为一位世界领导人，仁慈、有能力，接待其他即将来到中国的人，至少是以一种非常友好的方式。中国有句很古老的话，意思是万国都到这里来。习近平最近接待了很多领导人。

paras.en: DALY: He did very well from the Chinese point of view. I think that the hug of Donald Trump - we tend to see that from an American point of view as being friendly. Now, whether that's performative, friendship or truly felt is only for them to say. But for the Chinese, that's an unusually warm and humanizing move for Xi. Even the Chinese people will complain that their leaders are often too stayed, too in control. And this warmth, I think, also makes him look good, as does all the formal ceremony.
paras.zh: 戴利：从中国人的角度来看，他做得非常好。我认为唐纳德·特朗普的拥抱——从美国人的角度来看，我们倾向于认为这是友好的。现在，到底是表演的、友谊的还是真实的感受只有他们自己说了算。但对于中国人来说，习近平的这一举动异常温暖、人性化。甚至中国人也会抱怨他们的领导人常常过于保守、过于控制。我认为这种温暖也让他看起来很好，就像所有正式的仪式一样。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: We also had Vladimir Putin there, the president of Russia. What was his goal at this meeting?
paras.zh: 施密茨：我们还有俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京。他这次会议的目标是什么？

paras.en: DALY: Well, this appears to have been his idea. His goal as the head of what is now, at least in many spheres - not in China, but in the West - a rogue nation that has invaded Ukraine - he gets a place of honor with what are unquestionably the world's only two superpowers, but as if perhaps he's in their league, which, other than his possession of nuclear weapons, he really isn't.
paras.zh: 戴利：嗯，这似乎是他的主意。他的目标是作为现在的领导人，至少在许多领域——不是在中国，而是在西方——一个入侵乌克兰的流氓国家——他在无疑是世界上仅有的两个超级大国中获得了荣誉，但好像他可能属于他们的联盟，但除了拥有核武器之外，他实际上不是。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: Was he treated like he was in their league during this meeting?
paras.zh: 施密茨：在这次会议上，他受到的对待是否像他们的联盟一样？

paras.en: DALY: Well, this has been controversial within Russia itself. Some Russians on the internet have felt that he was dissed. He didn't get a meeting at the airport the way that Trump did. He didn't...
paras.zh: 戴利：嗯，这在俄罗斯内部一直存在争议。互联网上的一些俄罗斯人认为他受到了蔑视。他没有像特朗普那样在机场会面。他没有...

paras.en: DALY: ...Get bear hugged this time in public, although he has met with Xi Jinping about 50 times now. So he's been warmly greeted overall, but he didn't get quite the same status.
paras.zh: 达利：……尽管他已经与习近平会面了大约 50 次，但这次在公开场合受到了熊抱。所以他总体上受到了热烈的欢迎，但他并没有获得完全相同的地位。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: And it's important to point out here that, especially in Russia and in China, people often look for these symbolic gestures because there's not much to go on.
paras.zh: 施密茨：这里需要指出的是，特别是在俄罗斯和中国，人们经常寻找这些象征性的手势，因为没有太多可做的。

paras.en: China and Russia have called their partnership unbreakable in the past. Was that alliance meaningful at this summit?
paras.zh: 中国和俄罗斯过去曾称其伙伴关系牢不可破。这次峰会上的联盟有意义吗？

paras.en: DALY: Yes, and it has been meaningful really ever since the invasion of Ukraine. Tony Binken has said that China is the essential enabler for that invasion, both because it buys a lot of oil and gas, but also because it sells many, many dual-use parts to Russia, which enables it to improve its drones, but it also keeps it afloat economically.
paras.zh: 戴利：是的，自从入侵乌克兰以来，这确实很有意义。托尼·宾肯表示，中国是这次入侵的重要推动者，不仅因为它购买了大量石油和天然气，还因为它向俄罗斯出售许多很多军民两用零部件，这使其能够改进其无人机，同时也使其经济得以维持。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: I mentioned the small but significant detail that Xi met Trump on the runway. Did you spot any other moments at this summit that also caught your attention?
paras.zh: 施密茨：我提到了习近平在跑道上会见特朗普的一个小但重要的细节。您在本次峰会上还有其他引起您注意的时刻吗？

paras.en: DALY: After the meeting on the runway, what I was listening for was whether Xi Jinping would describe Trump as a great friend or a great and wise leader - all the things that Trump says about Xi, which are never reciprocated. Xi sort of pockets the compliment. He smiles...
paras.zh: 戴利：在跑道上的会面之后，我想听的是习近平是否会将特朗普描述为一位伟大的朋友或一位伟大而明智的领导人——特朗普对习近平所说的所有这些话，却从未得到回应。习近平似乎把这种恭维收入囊中。他微笑着...

paras.en: DALY: ...In an oracular way, and on we go. And so I was wondering, would that hug be followed up by protestations of friendship? And I didn't really hear that. And if you look at the Chinese government readout of the three-way meeting, it's just blandishments about the need for peace and friendship.
paras.zh: 戴利：……以一种神谕的方式，然后我们继续。所以我想知道，拥抱之后会伴随着友谊的表达吗？我并没有真正听到。如果你看一下中国政府对三方会议的宣读，你会发现这只是对和平与友谊的必要性的花言巧语。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: That's interesting. So what you noticed is something that actually didn't happen?
paras.zh: 施密茨：这很有趣。那么你注意到的是实际上没有发生的事情？

paras.en: DALY: He doesn't return the compliments.
paras.zh: 戴利：他没有回应这些赞美。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: What does that mean for the overall U.S.-China relationship in the eyes of someone like Xi Jinping, who's leading this country forward?
paras.zh: 施密茨：在像习近平这样领导这个国家前进的人眼中，这对整个美中关系意味着什么？

paras.en: DALY: Well, Xi, as I see it - he's not inclined to discuss his emotions or his feelings about even fellow Chinese ever.
paras.zh: 戴利：嗯，习近平，在我看来，他从来都不愿意讨论他的情绪或他对中国同胞的感受。

paras.en: DALY: There's a sense that as a leader of 1.4 billion, he should sort of be above personality...
paras.zh: DALY：有一种感觉，作为 14 亿人的领导者，他应该超越个性......

paras.en: DALY: ...And not show any of that. So it's part and parcel of that. But also if you compliment me and I don't return the compliment, there's a sense in which I win, right? At least in Chinese - in terms of Chinese political culture, that's true.
paras.zh: 戴利：……不要表现出任何这些。所以这是其中重要的一部分。但如果你赞美我而我没有回应你的赞美，那就有一种我赢了的感觉，对吧？至少在中国——就中国政治文化而言，确实如此。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: I sort of feel like this - were three leaders that were just saying, hey, how are you doing? You know, you look great. We're all great partners. And there wasn't really much something substantive coming out of this.
paras.zh: 施密茨：我有点像这样的感觉 - 三位领导人只是在说，嘿，你们好吗？你知道，你看起来很棒。我们都是很棒的合作伙伴。这并没有产生太多实质性的东西。

paras.en: DALY: President Trump did get them to speak publicly about nuclear weapons, and this gives a thin but an important foundation perhaps for later talks. China is nowhere near ready to talk about reducing its nuclear weapons. They continue to build and will until they get parity in about 10 years. But Xi Jinping did agree to talk about reducing nuclear risks. That's left vague, and they're talking about nonproliferation, but it opens the door. It opens the door a crack, and I think that's a good thing.
paras.zh: 戴利：特朗普总统确实让他们公开谈论核武器，这或许为以后的谈判提供了一个薄弱但重要的基础。中国还远未准备好谈论削减核武器。他们将继续建设，直到大约 10 年后实现平等。但习近平确实同意谈论减少核风险。这还很模糊，他们正在谈论防扩散，但它打开了大门。它打开了一条缝，我认为这是一件好事。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: Anything that maybe worried you about this summit?
paras.zh: 施密茨：本次峰会有什么让您担心的吗？

paras.en: DALY: Well, the question is, you know, whether President Trump is now setting a precedent for the way that other American leaders will behave vis-a-vis China. When you get these descriptions of friendship - Xi Jinping is a great leader, China is a great country - if the next guy doesn't repeat those phrases, then that will seem like a falling off.
paras.zh: 戴利：嗯，问题是，特朗普总统现在是否正在为其他美国领导人对待中国的方式树立先例。当你听到这些关于友谊的描述时——习近平是一位伟大的领导人，中国是一个伟大的国家——如果下一个人不重复这些短语，那么这就像是一种堕落。

paras.en: We seem to be going more and more for performance. In fact, all American presidents who have visited China have always been pleasant and respectful. Trump didn't invent this. But they've also described American interests, American values, America's dissatisfaction with China.
paras.zh: 我们似乎越来越注重性能。事实上，历任访问中国的美国总统都表现得和蔼可亲、恭敬有加。这不是特朗普发明的。但他们也描述了美国的利益、美国的价值观以及美国对中国的不满。

paras.en: And that's been OK. The Chinese don't expect the Americans to be exactly like them. But now Trump, I worry, is setting a precedent that makes it difficult to talk about the real problems we all face, and he doesn't seem to have done that at this meeting.
paras.zh: 那就没问题了。中国人并不期望美国人与他们完全一样。但我担心，现在特朗普正在开创一个先例，让我们很难谈论我们所有人面临的真正问题，而他在这次会议上似乎并没有这样做。

paras.en: SCHMITZ: That is Robert Daly. He's the director of the China and United States Program at University of Maryland School of Public Policy. Thanks so much for coming in.
paras.zh: 施密茨：那是罗伯特·戴利。他是马里兰大学公共政策学院中美项目主任。非常感谢您的光临。

paras.en: $100 cash rewards welcome offer -- New Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card holders can earn a $100 cash rewards welcome offer for spending just $500 in purchases in the first 3 months. Not only is this a very competitive sign-up bonus for a card with no annual fee, but it's also one of the things that sets this Wells Fargo credit card apart from other 2% back cards. We’ve yet to come across another credit card with 2% unlimited cash rewards that also has a sign-up bonus.
paras.zh: 100 美元现金奖励迎新优惠——新富国银行 Active Cash® 卡持卡人在前 3 个月内消费满 500 美元即可获得 100 美元现金奖励迎新优惠。对于一张免年费的卡来说，这不仅是非常有竞争力的开卡奖励，也是这张富国银行信用卡与其他 2% 返利卡不同的地方之一。我们还没有遇到过另一张既提供 2% 无限现金奖励又具有开卡奖励的信用卡。

paras.en: 12 months from account opening 0% APR intro offer -- New cardholders can enjoy 0% intro APR on both new purchases and qualifying balance transfers for a full 12 months from account opening. (After that period, a go-to rate of 18.74%, 24.74%, or 28.74% Variable APR applies.) That's a great offer, even when compared to cards marketed just for a 0% intro APR. It means that this card will allow you to avoid interest on purchases and balance transfers for a full year!
paras.zh: 开户后 12 个月内 0% 年利率介绍优惠——新持卡人可在开户后 12 个月内享受新购买和合格余额转账 0% 介绍年利率。 （在此期限之后，适用 18.74%、24.74% 或 28.74% 可变年利率的首选利率。）即使与仅以 0% 介绍年利率销售的卡相比，这也是一个很棒的优惠。这意味着这张卡可以让您免去一整年的购物利息和余额转账利息！

paras.en: No annual fee -- In many cases, high rewards rates mean high annual fees. Not with the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, which sports a $0 annual fee.
paras.zh: 无年费——很多情况下，高奖励率意味着高年费。富国银行 Active Cash® 卡则不然，该卡年费为 0 美元。

paras.en: Cell phone protection -- With the price of a typical cell phone in the hundreds of dollars, having some sort of insurance is a good idea. With this Wells Fargo card, you can get built-in cell phone protection of up to $600 just by paying your cell phone bill with your card. Coverage is subject to a $25 deductible.
paras.zh: 手机保护——普通手机的价格高达数百美元，购买某种保险是个好主意。有了这张富国银行卡，您只需用卡支付手机账单即可获得高达 600 美元的内置手机保护。承保范围需缴纳 25 美元的免赔额。

paras.en: Approval for the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card is most likely for applicants with good credit, which typically means a credit score of 670 or higher. If you need help rebuilding your credit, see this page.
paras.zh: 信用良好的申请人最有可能获得 Wells Fargo Active Cash® 卡的批准，这通常意味着信用评分为 670 或更高。如果您需要重建信用的帮助，请参阅此页面。

paras.en: We believe this is one of the best cash back cards for most people. Not only will you get a lucrative unlimited flat cash rewards rate, but it also sports a hefty, easy-to-earn sign-up bonus and a highly competitive 0% intro APR for 12 months from account opening on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, then 18.74%, 24.74%, or 28.74% Variable APR.
paras.zh: 我们相信这对大多数人来说是最好的现金返还卡之一。您不仅可以获得利润丰厚的无限固定现金奖励率，而且还可以享受易于赚取的巨额注册奖金和极具竞争力的 0% 介绍性年利率（自购买账户开户和合格余额转账起 12 个月），然后是 18.74%、24.74% 或 28.74% 可变年利率。

paras.en: Depending on what card is in your wallet today, there’s a high chance the Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card is a more lucrative upgrade -- and it could especially be an upgrade over debit cards, which have far worse fraud protections than credit cards and usually no rewards.
paras.zh: 根据您今天钱包里的卡类型，富国银行 Active Cash® 卡很可能是一种更有利可图的升级，尤其是借记卡的升级，借记卡的欺诈保护比信用卡差得多，而且通常没有奖励。
